purpose: Blinded source judgment of three linked Sima Bao claims in the Zhang Shi/Zhang Mao transition, including one earlier-life backstory; no proposed operations or desired verdicts included
question: Read all Chinese and independently judge each claim’s event owner and chronology. Distinguish the present 是歲 accession→Bao’s flight/interception/death sequence from the earlier 建興初 recruitment in Mao’s backstory. Preserve the explicit following 二年 and 太興三年 as separate event anchors; do not flatten the whole section to one era/year or create reign/lifespan intervals. Keep genuinely unresolved conversion/witness/owner conflicts. A supported one-sided bound is permissible; a missing exact year is not by itself a contradiction. No exact Bao death year may be imported without concrete primary evidence. Holds are valid.

value.unresolvedReason: s0242 遣其將陰監逆保 has no year. It follows s0234 是歲…建興六年 (AD 318) and precedes undated s0243 會保薨. Tongjian dates Bao's death 太興三年五月; Jin Shu does not close 320 as a second endpoint.
value.event: Sent to intercept Sima Bao, publicly as an escort but in truth to block his flight into Hexi.

value.unresolvedReason: s0257 writes 建興初, not 建興元年. 初 is an era-opening label, not year 1, and is not a closed AD 313 interval.
s0243 會保薨 has no year. It follows 保聞湣帝崩 and the 是歲 / 太興 accession (AD 318) and supplies no later Chinese year such as 太興三年.
value.event: Died while planning to flee to Zhang Shi; more than ten thousand of his followers drifted into Liangzhou.

hints: AD 318+ (after 湣帝崩 / 會保薨)
AD 318+ (onOrAfter 是歲 太興 / 建興六年; 逆保 undated)

units.zh: 軍次新陽，會湣帝崩問至，素服舉哀，大臨三日。
units.en: Camped at Xinyang, they learned of Emperor Min’s death, donned mourning, and wailed three days.
units.literal: The army halted at Xinyang; just then news arrived that Emperor Min had died; they put on white garments and observed mourning, holding grand lament for three days.

units.zh: 時南陽王保謀稱尊號，破羌都尉張詵言於寔曰：「南陽王忘莫大之恥，而欲自尊，天不受其圖籙，德不足以應運，終非濟時救難者也。
units.en: At that time Prince of Nanyang Sima Bao plotted to assume the imperial style; Colonel Who Breaks the Qiang Zhang Shen said to Shi, ‘The Prince of Nanyang forgets the greatest shame yet wishes to exalt himself; Heaven will not accept his talisman charts, and his virtue is not enough to answer the season—he is not one who can save the age from disaster.
units.literal: At that time Prince of Nanyang Sima Bao plotted to assume the imperial style; Colonel Who Breaks the Qiang Zhang Shen said to Shi, ‘The Prince of Nanyang forgets the greatest shame yet wishes to exalt himself; Heaven will not accept his talisman charts, and his virtue is not enough to answer the season—he is not one who can save the age from disaster.

units.zh: 晉王明德昵籓，先帝憑屬，宜表稱聖德，勸即尊號，傳檄諸籓，副言相府，則欲競之心息，未合之徒散矣。」
units.en: The Prince of Jin is illustrious in virtue and intimate with the feudatories; the late emperor relied on him—you ought to memorialize his sagely virtue, urge him to take the supreme title, circulate a manifesto to the princes, and send duplicate word to the minister’s headquarters; then hearts that would compete will rest and factions not yet united will scatter.’
units.literal: The Prince of Jin is illustrious in virtue and intimate with the feudatories; the late emperor relied on him—you ought to memorialize his sagely virtue, urge him to take the supreme title, circulate a manifesto to the princes, and send duplicate word to the minister’s headquarters; then hearts that would compete will rest and factions not yet united will scatter.’

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: Zhang Shi agreed.
units.literal: Shi followed this.

units.zh: 於是馳檄天下，推崇晉王為天子，遣牙門蔡忠奉表江南，勸即尊位。
units.en: He broadcast a call to crown Sima Rui as emperor and sent Cai Zhong to the south with a memorial urging accession.
units.literal: Thereupon he sped a manifesto through the realm, exalting the Prince of Jin as Son of Heaven, sent gate guard Cai Zhong with a memorial south of the Yangzi, and urged him to mount the throne.

units.zh: 是歲，元帝即位於建鄴，改年太興，寔猶稱建興六年，不從中興之所改也。
units.en: That year Yuan Di took the throne at Jianye as Taixing; Zhang Shi still dated documents Jianxing year six, refusing the new era.
units.literal: That year Yuan Di mounted the throne at Jianye and changed the era name to Taixing; Shi still used the sixth year of Jianxing and did not follow the change made for the restoration.

units.zh: 保聞湣帝崩，自稱晉王，建元，署置百官，遣使拜寔征西大將軍、儀同三司，增邑三千戶。
units.en: Sima Bao then styled himself prince of Jin, set up a court calendar, and offered Zhang Shi the western-conquest generalship with three thousand extra households.
units.literal: When Bao heard that Emperor Min had died, he styled himself Prince of Jin, established an era title, appointed the full set of officials, and sent envoys to appoint Shi as Grand General Who Conquers the West with ceremonies matching the Three Excellencies, increasing his fief by three thousand households.

units.zh: 俄而保為陳安所叛，氐羌皆應之。
units.en: Chen An soon rebelled against him, joined by Di and Qiang.
units.literal: Soon Bao was betrayed by Chen An, and the Di and Qiang all responded to him.

units.zh: 保窘迫，遂去上邽，遷祁山，寔遣將韓璞步騎五千赴難。
units.en: Bao fled to Qishan; Zhang Shi sent Han Pu with five thousand men.
units.literal: Bao was hard pressed, thereupon left Shanggui, and moved to Qishan; Shi sent General Han Pu with five thousand foot and horse to answer the crisis.

units.zh: 陳安退保綿諸，保歸上邽。
units.en: Chen An fell back to Mianzhu while Bao reoccupied Shanggui.
units.literal: Chen An withdrew to defend Mianzhu; Bao returned to Shanggui.

units.zh: 未幾，保復為安所敗，使詣寔乞師。
units.en: Soon Bao lost again to Chen An and begged Zhang Shi for an army.
units.literal: Before long Bao was again defeated by An and sent to Shi begging for troops.

units.zh: 寔遣宋毅赴之，而安退。
units.en: Zhang Shi dispatched Song Yi, and Chen An retreated.
units.literal: Shi sent Song Yi to go to him, and An withdrew.

units.zh: 會保為劉曜所逼，遷于桑城，將謀奔寔。
units.en: Then Liu Yao drove Bao to Sangcheng, and he meant to run to Hexi.
units.literal: Just then Bao was hard pressed by Liu Yao, moved to Sangcheng, and planned to flee to Shi.

units.zh: 寔以其宗室之望，若至河右，必動物情，遣其將陰監逆保，聲言翼衛，實禦之也。
units.en: Zhang Shi feared a royal prince on his soil would sway the people, so he sent Yin Jian to “escort” him while actually blocking his flight.
units.literal: Shi, because Bao enjoyed prestige as a member of the imperial clan, feared that if he reached the west of the river he would stir popular feeling; he sent his general Yin Jian to intercept Bao, declaring publicly that he meant to shield him but in truth blocking him.

units.zh: 會保薨，其眾散奔涼州者萬餘人。
units.en: Bao died; over ten thousand of his followers drifted into Liangzhou.
units.literal: Just then Bao died; more than ten thousand of his host scattered and fled into Liangzhou.

units.zh: 寔自恃險遠，頗自驕恣。
units.en: Secure in his remoteness, Zhang Shi grew proud and lax.
units.literal: Shi, relying on the danger and distance of his position, became rather arrogant and self-indulgent.

units.zh: 初，寔寢室梁間有人像，無頭，久而乃滅，寔甚惡之。
units.en: A headless figure had appeared between the rafters of his bedroom and faded away—an omen he loathed.
units.literal: In the beginning, in Shi’s bedchamber a headless human form appeared between the beams; after a long while it vanished; Shi greatly hated it.

units.zh: 京兆人劉弘者，挾左道，客居天梯第五山，然燈懸鏡於山穴中為光明，以惑百姓，受道者千餘人，寔左右皆事之。
units.en: Liu Hong of Jingzhao peddled sorcery on Tianti’s Fifth Mountain, dazzled villagers with lamps and mirrors, and drew even Zhang Shi’s household into his sect.
units.literal: There was a man of Jingzhao, Liu Hong, who practiced heterodox arts, lodged as a guest on the fifth terrace of Mount Tian ladder, hung lamps and mirrors in a mountain cave to make light, and deluded the common people; more than a thousand received his teaching, and Shi’s attendants on left and right all served him.

units.zh: 帳下閻沙、牙門趙仰皆弘鄉人，弘謂之曰：「天與我神璽，應王涼州。」
units.en: Camp guard Yan Sha and gate guard Zhao Yang were fellow townsmen of Hong; Hong said to them, ‘Heaven has given me a divine seal—I ought to rule Liangzhou."
units.literal: Camp guard Yan Sha and gate guard Zhao Yang were fellow townsmen of Hong; Hong said to them, ‘Heaven has given me a divine seal—I ought to rule Liangzhou.

units.zh: 沙、仰信之，密與寔左右十餘人謀殺寔，奉弘為主。
units.en: They conspired with Zhang Shi’s guards to murder him and enthrone Liu Hong.
units.literal: Sha and Yang believed him and secretly plotted with more than ten of Shi’s attendants to kill Shi and set up Hong as lord.

units.zh: 寔潛知其謀，收弘殺之。
units.en: Zhang Shi uncovered the plot, arrested Hong, and killed him.
units.literal: Shi secretly learned of the plot, seized Hong, and executed him.

units.zh: 沙等不之知，以其夜害寔。
units.en: Yan Sha’s party, unaware, struck that night and killed Zhang Shi.
units.literal: Sha and the others did not know this; that night they murdered Shi.

units.zh: 在位六年。
units.en: He had held power six years.
units.literal: He had occupied the position six years.

units.zh: 私諡曰昭公，元帝賜諡曰元。
units.en: Privately he was called Duke Zhao; Emperor Yuan gave him the posthumous name Yuan.
units.literal: Privately he was posthumously titled Duke Zhao; Yuan Di granted the posthumous title Yuan.

units.zh: 子駿，年幼，弟茂攝事。
units.en: His son Zhang Jun was a child, so his brother Zhang Mao took the reins.
units.literal: His son Jun was young; younger brother Mao took charge of affairs.

units.zh: 寔弟茂
units.en: Zhang Mao, Zhang Shi’s younger brother
units.literal: Younger brother of Shi: Mao

units.zh: =茂字成遜，虛靖好學，不以世利嬰心。
units.en: Zhang Mao, courtesy name Chengxun, lived plainly, loved books, and shunned gain.
units.literal: = Mao, courtesy name Chengxun, was empty and still, fond of learning, and did not let worldly profit entangle his mind.

units.zh: 建興初，南陽王保辟從事中郎，又薦為散騎侍郎、中壘將軍，皆不就。
units.en: Sima Bao summoned him as staff officer and recommended court posts; he declined all.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jianxing era Prince of Nanyang Sima Bao summoned him as an aide-de-camp; he also recommended him as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and general of the central rampart, but in neither case did he take office.

units.zh: 二年，徵為侍中，以父老固辭。
units.en: In year two he was called to be palace attendant but cited his father’s age and refused.
units.literal: In the second year he was summoned as palace attendant but firmly declined on account of his father’s age.

units.zh: 尋拜平西將軍、秦州刺史。
units.en: He was soon named general who pacifies the west and inspector of Qinzhou.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qinzhou.

units.zh: 太興三年，寔既遇害，州人推茂為大都督、太尉、涼州牧，茂不從，但受使持節、平西將軍、涼州牧。
units.en: After Zhang Shi’s murder the province offered Mao the grand governorship; he took only the staff and western pacification title.
units.literal: In the third year of Taixing, after Shi had met murder, the people of the province urged Mao as grand governor, grand commandant, and governor of Liangzhou; Mao did not accept but took only the credentials, the title General Who Pacifies the West, and governor of Liangzhou.
